title: "Sparse-LD and individual-level workflows"

This page connects the maintained packed-BED and summary-statistics workflows.
For matrix definitions, CSR storage, and alignment assumptions, see
[Sparse-LD CSR methods](../methods/sparse_ld_csr.qmd).

## Two data levels

The individual-level route keeps the analysed packed genotypes available to
the sampler:

```r
fit_bed <- stblr_bed(
  y = y,
  Glist = Glist,
  method = "bayesc",
  nit = 1000,
  nburn = 500,
  seed = 1
)
```

The summary-statistics route derives aligned sufficient statistics and an LD
operator first:

```r
stats <- make_summary_stats(Glist = Glist, y = y)
Glist <- make_sparse_ld(Glist = Glist)

fit_csr <- stblr_csr(
  stats = stats,
  Glist = Glist,
  method = "sbayesc",
  nit = 1000,
  nburn = 500,
  seed = 1
)
```

The `s` prefix identifies summary-statistics models. It does not activate
`selection_s`. Use `sbayesr` instead of `sbayesc` for the summary-statistics
BayesR prior kernel.

## Alignment contract

The following order must agree exactly:

1. rows of `stats$wy` and `stats$ww`;
2. rows and columns of the sparse-LD operator;
3. `fit$data$marker_metadata`;
4. annotation rows when annotations are used;
5. marker-indexed starting states and optional `selection_maf`.

Use stable marker IDs. Never silently intersect or reorder external statistics,
LD, or annotations without an exact identifier match. The same analysed
individuals, genotype scaling, allele orientation, and marker order should be
used when constructing matched BED and summary-statistics comparisons.

## Block-eigen summary operator

`stblr_block_eigen()` uses the same summary-statistics model names and builds a
represented LD operator from the supplied genotype provenance:

```r
fit_block <- stblr_block_eigen(
  stats = stats,
  Glist = Glist,
  block_start = 1L,
  method = "sbayesc"
)
```

Filtering changes the represented operator. Exact CSR/block-eigen reductions
therefore require the documented unfiltered reconstruction setup.

## Annotation-aware summary fitting

Annotation policies are selected independently of the summary model name:

```r
fit_fixed <- stblr_csr_annot(
  stats = stats,
  Glist = Glist,
  annotations = fixed_prior_spec,
  annotation_model = "fixed_marker",
  method = "sbayesc"
)

fit_probit <- stblr_csr_annot(
  stats = stats,
  Glist = Glist,
  annotations = annotation_matrix,
  annotation_model = "annotation_probit_stick",
  method = "sbayesrc",
  mixture_var = c(0, 0.01, 0.1, 1)
)
```

The other BayesC annotation policies are `group` and `learned_logistic`.
Annotations and `selection_s` are separate dimensions: annotations affect
probability policies, while `selection_s` optionally scales effect variance by
MAF.

## Multi-trait routes

Use `mtblr_bed()` with `bayesc`, `bayesr`, or `bayesrc` for individual-level
data. Use `mtblr_csr()` or `mtblr_block_eigen()` with `sbayesc`, `sbayesr`, or
`sbayesrc` for summary statistics. Summary routes do not infer missing
cross-trait information that is absent from their input contract.

appropriate chain lengths, memory review, convergence diagnostics, and
sensitivity analysis.
